headline: A 2026 AK91 replaces the constant Mincer return with a time-varying skill price rho_t = (1/sigma)(D_t - s_t): trained only on 2005-2014, this supply-demand model forecasts the entire 2015-2024 return decline (held-out RMSE 0.0049) that the original constant-return model (0.0398) and a naive trend (0.0259) get wrong.

tables.title: Race decomposition of the change in the return (sigma=2)

figures.caption: AK91, theory updated to 2026. Panel A: the return to schooling is a time-varying skill price, not the constant of the original model (gray dashed); package anchors (1970/1980) and ACS 2005-2024 rise to a 0.12 peak then fall, the updated supply-demand model (green) tracks it, and the held-out (2015-2024) naive trend extrapolation (orange dotted) runs the wrong way. Panel B: the race between education and technology -- demand push (orange) vs education-supply drag (blue) by era, with the net change in rho; supply overtakes demand after 2012.
figures.alt: Two panels. Left: return to schooling vs year; two black diamonds near 0.07/0.063 at 1970/1980, a blue ACS curve from 0.108 (2005) up to 0.120 (2012) down to 0.092 (2024), a flat gray dashed line at 0.063 labeled original model, a green model line tracking the blue, and an orange dotted line rising into a shaded 2015-2024 held-out band. Right: stacked bars for 1980-2005, 2005-2012, 2012-2024 with positive orange demand bars and negative blue supply bars and black net-change dots at +0.045, +0.012, -0.028.

notes: sigma=2.0 is CALIBRATED (Katz-Murphy/AKK range and held-out-optimal), not structurally estimated; all decomposition signs are invariant for sigma in {1.5,2.0,2.5}.
Supply is proxied by the men-40-49 sample's own college log-odds (internally consistent), not the economy-wide college-equivalent series; the aggregate SBTC narrative is PROPOSED/cite-level.

Reused 001's return series, weak-IV objects (F/AR/Q1), and enrollment; new compute was only 9 benchmark ACS re-extractions for schooling-supply moments (return checks reproduce 001 to 4 decimals). 2020 ACS absent (Census COVID gap).

A 2026 QOB-style paper would need a college-margin instrument (aid/tuition/admission discontinuities or state 16->18 dropout-age changes) strong enough to clear F>>10; QOB is exhausted (enrollment 0.97). [PROPOSED design.]
